messages:
jamal: Quick pulse — rerunning continuous-batching fairness probe with the replay harness after the recent kernel selector change. Observed p99 tail spikes for some tenants when kernel_policy=auto, especially under KV-heavy traces.

maria: Can you share the exact replay command and config you used?

jamal: Sure — command I ran:
```bash
./replay_harness \
  --trace s3://redwood-replays/2026-03/kv-heavy-multi-tenant.json \
  --concurrency 60 \
  --arrival poisson --seed 42 \
  --max-delay-ms 12 \
  --batch-cap 64 \
  --kernel-policy auto \
  --tenant-mix "[0.5,0.2,0.15,0.1,0.05]"
```

sophia: Noted. From the runtime logs the selector did fall back to an int8 fallback kernel for long sequences: `matmul-int8-fallback` shows up a lot when avg_seq_len>1024. Profiler snippet from the same run: 
```text
kernel_selector: selected=matmul-fp16 duration_ms=1.4
kv_cache_hit_rate=0.82
avg_queue_delay_ms=6.3
p50_ms=24.1 p95_ms=110.2 p99_ms=280.6
```

perf-bot: CI replay/job #r-5621 finished — artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/r-5621/ (perf CSV + traces) :white_check_mark:

jamal: My hypothesis: when kernel selector flips to int8 fallback it increases per-token compute variance which, combined with large batchcap, lets some tenants' requests wait behind heavy long-seq batches -> KV cache evictions and thrashing. Need apples-to-apples across kernel choices.

kai: Agreed. For apples-to-apples we should: 1) pin kernel via a runtime flag (e.g., `--force-kernel matmul-fp16`), 2) freeze quant profile, 3) replay identical streams (same seed + same arrival distribution).

maria: Also add a tenant-weighted fairness metric. Suggest: `tail_unfairness_ratio_t = p99_tenant / p99_global` computed per-tenant, plus a single-number summary `unfairness_index = max(ratios) / median(ratios)`.

sophia: Ran quick micro-sweep this afternoon (small matrix):
```text
config A: batchcap=64 max_delay=12 kernel=auto 
fairness_ratios=[1.9,1.2,1.1,2.6,1.0]
cost_delta= +4.8%

config B: batchcap=16 max_delay=2 kernel=matmul-fp16 
fairness_ratios=[1.05,1.02,1.01,1.09,1.00]
cost_delta= +12.3%
```
Interpretation: smaller batchcap / lower max_delay reduces unfairness at expense of higher per-token cost.

jamal: That's exactly the tradeoff. We need to quantify where the knee is for real workloads and decide a policy: either per-tenant batch caps or adaptive caps based on recent KV hit rates.

kai: Proposal: implement `--tenant-batch-cap` override where high-traffic tenants get smaller caps during bursts, plus a `kv-hit-threshold` to relax caps when hit rate > 0.8. We can A/B this in a dedicated sweep.

maria: Action items: 
1) jamal: add `--force-kernel` and `--tenant-batch-cap` flags to the replay/runtime (PR by EOD Thu).
2) kai & sophia: extend replay harness to orchestrate mixed-tenancy bursts and emit per-tenant p50/p95/p99 + fairness metrics (overnight sweep).
3) jamal: run an apples-to-apples sweep (auto vs pinned-fp16 vs pinned-int8) with seeds {42,99,2026} and upload CSVs to s3://redwood-perf/continuous-batching/exp-2026-03-22/

jamal: I'll start the runtime flag PR now and post a draft link.

perf-bot: Created perf issue #INF-1142 with checklist and links to artifacts.

maria: Please include a short note in the PR about how KV cache eviction metrics are computed (sample window, keys evicted/sec). We need consistent definitions for the sweep.

sophia: Will do. For reference, my eviction calc is: `evictions_per_min = evicted_keys / (sample_seconds/60)`, window=300s.

jamal: Draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/3892 — flags added, basic unit tests. Starting the overnight sweep now.

kai: If sweep shows >2x unfairness for any tenant under `kernel=auto`, we should default to `kernel=matmul-fp16` for multi-tenant pools until we ship adaptive caps.

maria: Sounds good. Add a follow-up to sync with product on cost vs fairness tradeoff before we change defaults.

jamal: Sweep kicked off — ETA ~8h. Uploading logs to s3 when done. Thanks all :pray:

sophia: Thanks — will watch the sweep and start analysis scripts. :mag_right:

maria: Great work. We'll review results tomorrow at the runtime standup. :calendar:
